analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analysed health examination data of 1,287,412 women in Guangdong Province, China, from 2016 to 2022, using tree distributed lag non-linear models to evaluate lagged associations with HPV positivity.
analysis.methods: Ten covariates were collected, and temperature, particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5), and normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) were assigned by examination date. Tree distributed lag non-linear models were applied to evaluate lagged associations with HPV positivity at screening.
analysis.main_results: Low temperature was associated with higher cumulative odds of HPV positivity at shorter lags (cOR = 1.303, 95% CrI, 1.194, 1.428), whereas high temperature showed a longer-lag association at longer lags (cOR = 1.063, 95% CrI, 1.007, 1.122). High PM2.5 and low NDVI were associated with higher odds of HPV positivity over various lag weeks.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified pre-screening environmental correlates of HPV positivity, with stronger associations for low temperature at shorter lags and high temperature at longer lags. High PM2.5 and low NDVI were also associated with higher odds in the primary 24-week analyses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that environmental factors, particularly temperature and air pollution, may influence HPV positivity and warrant confirmation in longitudinal studies with repeated HPV testing and more comprehensive control of temporal, spatial, behavioral, and socioeconomic factors.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's design limitations include the use of cross-sectional data and potential confounding factors. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the need for longitudinal confirmation.

It found that low temperature was associated with higher HPV positivity at shorter lags, while high temperature showed a longer-lag association. High PM2.5 and low NDVI were also associated with higher odds of HPV positivity.

papers.title_zh: 筛选时温度、颗粒物和绿度与 人乳头瘤病毒 阳性的关联:使用树状分布滞后非线性模型对广东省(2016-2022 年)的分析
papers.source_body_en: Introduction Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a double-stranded DNA virus that may cause cervical, vulvar, and anal cancers in women. Environmental factors including temperature, air pollution, and greenness may be associated with HPV positivity; however, evidence remains limited. Methods This study analysed health examination data of 1,287,412 women in Guangdong Province, China (2016-2022). Ten covariates were collected, and temperature, particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5), and normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) were assigned by examination date. Tree distributed lag non-linear models were applied to evaluate lagged associations with HPV positivity at screening. Results Using the Q50 of biweekly mean temperature, PM2.5, and NDVI (25.594°C, 20.300 μg/m3, and 0.544, respectively) as references, low temperature (Q2.5, 13.300°C) was associated with higher cumulative odds of HPV positivity at Lag Weeks 3-8 (cOR = 1.303, 95% CrI, 1.194, 1.428), whereas high temperature (Q97.5, 29.851°C) showed a longer-lag association at Lag Weeks 9-14 (cOR = 1.063, 95% CrI, 1.007, 1.122). High PM2.5 (Q97.5, 38.021μg/m3) and low NDVI (Q2.5, 0.229) were associated with higher odds of HPV positivity over Lag Weeks 1-16 (cOR = 1.172, 95% CrI, 1.051, 1.283) and Lag Weeks 5-18 (cOR = 1.318, 95% CrI, 1.131, 1.566), respectively. Stratified analyses suggested stronger low-temperature associations among middle-aged and older women and among women in the Pearl River Delta and Western Guangdong. Discussion In conclusion, temperature showed lag-dependent associations with screening-detected HPV positivity, with stronger associations for low temperature at shorter lags and high temperature at longer lags. High PM2.5 and low NDVI were also associated with higher odds in the primary 24-week analyses. Temporal sensitivity analyses attenuated the PM2.5 association and weakened the NDVI association under the 36-week specification, whereas the low-temperature association was comparatively stable and uncertainty increased for high temperature. These findings identify pre-screening environmental correlates of HPV positivity and warrant confirmation in longitudinal studies with repeated HPV testing and more comprehensive control of temporal, spatial, behavioral, and socioeconomic factors.

papers.title: Impact of menopausal status on human papillomavirus detection and cervical neoplasia in middle-aged Senegalese women
papers.abstract: Hormonal and immunologic changes related to menopause may play a role in human papillomavirus (HPV) and cervical neoplasia detection, yet this relationship has not been examined in West African populations, where cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related death. The purpose of this study was to assess whether menopausal status is associated with HPV and cervical neoplasia detection in Senegalese women aged 40–60. We conducted a secondary analysis of three prospective cervical cancer studies in Dakar, Senegal (1998–2011). Participants with known menopausal status and a satisfactory HPV test (N = 3,118) and/or Pap smear (N = 2,907) were included, excluding those with cervical cancer or pregnancy; participants without known HIV status were additionally excluded from the cervical neoplasia analysis. Multivariable logistic regression and generalized estimating equations were used to estimate adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for age, gravidity, and HIV status. Compared with premenopausal women, postmenopausal women had significantly higher odds of HPV detection (OR = 1.48; 95% CI: 1.18, 1.85), including both high-risk (OR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.25, 1.93) and low-risk types (OR = 1.64; 95% CI: 1.30, 2.08). Odds of cervical neoplasia were elevated, but non-significant, among postmenopausal women (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 0.97, 1.90), with increased odds for both high-grade (OR = 1.43; 95% CI: 0.90, 2.28) and low-grade lesions (OR = 1.30; 95% CI: 0.84, 2.02). However, in a sensitivity analysis restricted to participants with known HIV status, these cervical neoplasia odds were attenuated, suggesting caution in interpreting the magnitude of these findings. These findings suggest menopause may contribute to HPV persistence or reactivation, and development of cervical neoplasia. Our results highlight the importance of continued surveillance for HPV and cervical neoplasia among older women, particularly in low-resource settings with disproportionately high cervical cancer burden.

papers.title_zh: 绝经状态对塞内加尔中年妇女 人乳头瘤病毒 检测和宫颈肿瘤的影响
papers.source_body_en: Hormonal and immunologic changes related to menopause may play a role in human papillomavirus (HPV) and cervical neoplasia detection, yet this relationship has not been examined in West African populations, where cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related death. The purpose of this study was to assess whether menopausal status is associated with HPV and cervical neoplasia detection in Senegalese women aged 40–60. We conducted a secondary analysis of three prospective cervical cancer studies in Dakar, Senegal (1998–2011). Participants with known menopausal status and a satisfactory HPV test (N = 3,118) and/or Pap smear (N = 2,907) were included, excluding those with cervical cancer or pregnancy; participants without known HIV status were additionally excluded from the cervical neoplasia analysis. Multivariable logistic regression and generalized estimating equations were used to estimate adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for age, gravidity, and HIV status. Compared with premenopausal women, postmenopausal women had significantly higher odds of HPV detection (OR = 1.48; 95% CI: 1.18, 1.85), including both high-risk (OR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.25, 1.93) and low-risk types (OR = 1.64; 95% CI: 1.30, 2.08). Odds of cervical neoplasia were elevated, but non-significant, among postmenopausal women (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 0.97, 1.90), with increased odds for both high-grade (OR = 1.43; 95% CI: 0.90, 2.28) and low-grade lesions (OR = 1.30; 95% CI: 0.84, 2.02). However, in a sensitivity analysis restricted to participants with known HIV status, these cervical neoplasia odds were attenuated, suggesting caution in interpreting the magnitude of these findings. These findings suggest menopause may contribute to HPV persistence or reactivation, and development of cervical neoplasia. Our results highlight the importance of continued surveillance for HPV and cervical neoplasia among older women, particularly in low-resource settings with disproportionately high cervical cancer burden.

papers.title: Association of Receipt of Human Papillomavirus Vaccination and Personal History of Cancer Diagnosis in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study Using NHIS Data
papers.abstract: Background: Cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing subsequent cancers, including HPV-associated cancers, compared to the general population. However, evidence regarding the receipt of HPV vaccination and cancer diagnosis status is limited. Methods: We analyzed 2019 and 2022 National Health Interview Survey data, focusing on adults aged 18–45 years who were eligible for HPV vaccination. We performed descriptive statistics and evaluated associations using survey-weighted bivariable and multivariable logistic regression to assess the association between a personal history of any cancer diagnosis and receipt of HPV vaccination, adjusting for sociodemographic and behavioral factors. Results: Among 20,917 participants (mean [SD] age (years): 31.41 [13.58]), 489 (2.0%) were cancer survivors; 99 (19.3%) received HPV vaccination. Among 20,423 adults without a cancer diagnosis, 5317 (27.8%) had received HPV vaccination. Five participants had missing data on cancer history. Cancer survivors had significantly lower odds of HPV vaccination compared to adults without a personal cancer history (Adjusted Odds Ratio [aOR]: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.52–0.87, p = 0.003). Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) were synthesized and their optical properties characterized using UV–Vis spectroscopy. Subsequently, the plasmon response was evaluated in the presence of HPV biomolecules. Results indicate a shift in the resonance wavelength, suggesting a direct interaction that could be exploited for the design of highly sensitive sensors. This study contributes to biomedical applications for early virus detection through nanomaterials. papers.full_text: Conference Abstracts - 8th International Cancer Congress Vol. 6, Issue Supplement 2, 2026 · S1-2 Prevalence, Genotype Distribution, Risk Factors and Treatment of Cervical Human Papillomavirus Infection among Women in Dharan Municipality Anjal Shah, MBBS,Ramesh Shrestha, MBBS, MD Submission received: 2026-08-16 / Accepted: 2026-08-27 / Published: 2026-09-11 Abstract Background In this study we aimed to determine the overall and type-specific prevalence of cervical human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, risk factors for such infection among women in Dharan Municipality, and treatment of those with HPV infection. Methods It was a descriptive observational study conducted among 3857 married women aged 30-60 years in 18 wards (Ward no. 1to 20 except 4 and 7) of Dharan Municipality, Province 1, Nepal in July, 2024. Sociodemographic data and information on risk factors for cervical cancer were obtained through an interview. Cervicovaginal swab was collected for HPV DNA detection (both physician assisted and self sampling). HPV DNA testing was done in Provincial(province one) Health Laboratory (PHL) at Biratnagar by Jiangsu Macro-Micro test kit using the platform of Q-Tower 3 Analytica Jena. It was a multiplex assay and the HPV types detected were HPV 16, HPV 18, and other hrHPV (HPV 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68). Triaging was done with VIA, conventional PAP smear and/or colposcopy for those with HPV DNA positive women. Treatment was done with thermocoagulation or LEEP for those with abnormal triage results but advised for close follow up at 1-2years if the triage results were normal. Results Among them, 161 women had hrHPV infection and 186 cervicovaginal samples had inconclusive reports accounting for the HPV prevalence rate of 4.39% (161/3671). HPV16 positivity was seen in 42.9%(69/161) women, HPV 18 positivity in 8.1%(13/161), other hrHPV positivity in 55.3%(89/161), and co-infection in 6.2%(10/161) women. 186 samples had inconclusive reports. Only eleven among 161 HPV positive women had previously been screened in their lifetime. HPV infection was associated with early age at marriage, early age at first child birth, multiparity, and current smoking. Among 161 HPV positive women, only 100 women had followed up for triage test (VIA triage=92, PAP cytology triage=8) while rest of the 61 women did not follow up for triage testing. Among 100 women undergoing triage testing, 47 women were VIA positive, 45 women were VIA negative and 8 women had PAP cytology as NILM. Among 47 women with VIA positivity, acetowhite lesions was seen in the anterior lip in 34 women, posterior lips in 10 women and both lips in 3 women respectively. Among 47 women with VIA positivity, nine women had undergone colposcopy triage before treatment. Among nine women with colposcopy triage, six women underwent LEEP procedure (1 women=SCC, HSIL=4 women, LSIL=1 women) and four women had thermocoagulation. Altogether, 41 women fulfilling the eligible criteria were ablated with thermocoagulation (38 women after VIA triage, 3 women after VIA and/or colposcopy triage). One women with SCC underwent laparoscopic radical hysterectomy for early stage disease. Conclusion This is the first population-based study to report the prevalence, risk factors and treatment of cervical HPV infection from eastern part of Nepal.

papers.title: A Multimethod Evaluation to Assess Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Efficacy of HPVVaxFacts, a Tailored Mobile Web App, for Parents With Unvaccinated Children: Pilot 2-Arm Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Mobile health (mHealth) interventions may improve provider-parent communication on human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination to reduce concerns, and increase intention and uptake. HPVVaxFacts (233 Analytics) is a novel, mobile web app delivering tailored education based on the Health Belief Model and Theory of Reasoned Action, addressing parental concerns preclinic visit. Objective This study aimed to assess the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of HPVVaxFacts among parents of adolescents aged 9‐17 years. Methods We conducted a pilot, randomized controlled trial in 2 urban Tennessee clinics from June to September 2023 comparing 2 groups: tailored education via HPVVaxFacts mobile web app (intervention, n=27), and nutrition education (attention control, n=30). Eligible parents had or were caregivers to a child aged 9 to 17 years unvaccinated against HPV, had a mobile phone, had an upcoming clinic visit, and spoke English. The recruitment strategy was patient intake software—Phreesia (Phreesia, Inc ) and eClinicalWorks (eClinicalWorks). Although unblinded, parents could deduce their study arm assignment. Providers were blinded. Feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy (HPV vaccine knowledge, concerns, intentions, and vaccination rates) were assessed using multimethod evaluation. Parents were assessed at baseline and immediately post intervention via surveys. Vaccination rates were assessed at 12 months post intervention via electronic health records. Nineteen parent interviews were conducted up to 9 months post intervention. A clinic staff consultation (n=6) was 1 month post intervention. Results Of 57 enrolled parents, most were female (52/57, 91%), non-Hispanic White (44/57, 77%), had ≤US $80,000 household income (32/57, 56%), and had some college or less (27/57, 47%). In total, 81% (36) of parents viewed HPVVaxFacts. Post intervention, HPV vaccine initiation was higher in the intervention group compared to the attention control group (48% vs 17%; difference 0.24; 95% CI 0.03-0.46; P =.01). Parents in the HPVVaxFacts arm demonstrated a greater reduction in knowledge (ie, knowledge increase; mean change: −0.6 vs 0.1) and concern scores (mean change: −3.4 vs −1.4) than those in the nutrition education arm. However, between-arm differences were not statistically significant ( P =.13 and P =.14, respectively). The majority found the study protocol and HPVVaxFacts acceptable. Benefits of HPVVaxFacts include confirming their decision to vaccinate, supporting parent-child discussion on the vaccine, and answering questions preclinic visit or offering questions for the provider. Study protocol delivery and mobile web app instructions were suggested areas for improvement. Barriers for HPVVaxFacts use include content in English only and digital format. Conclusions Our study suggests HPVVaxFacts was feasible and acceptable among parents to provide previsit, tailored information on HPV vaccination. Outcomes offer a positive trajectory but need more exploration. Next steps include a well-powered efficacy trial to determine the impact of HPVVaxFacts on initiation vaccine rates and parental hesitancy factors, as well as to explore an interaction, effect modification, and mediation among different variables.

papers.title: Serum, cell-free, HPV-human DNA junction detection and HPV typing for predicting and monitoring cervical cancer recurrence.
papers.abstract: Almost all cervical cancers are caused by human papillomaviruses (HPVs). In most cases, HPV DNA is integrated into the human genome. We found that tumor-specific, HPV-human DNA junctions are detectable in serum cell-free DNA of a fraction of cervical cancer patients at the time of initial treatment and/or at 6 months following treatment. Retrospective analysis revealed these junctions were more frequently detectable in women in whom the cancer later recurred. We also found that cervical cancers caused by HPV types outside of phylogenetic clade α9 had a higher recurrence frequency than those caused by α9 types in both our study and The Cancer Genome Atlas cervical cancer database, despite the higher prevalence ofα9 types, including HPV16, in cervical cancer. Thus, HPV-human DNA junction detection in serum cell-free DNA and HPV type determination in tumor tissue may help predict recurrence risk. Screening serum cell-free DNA for junctions may also offer an unambiguous non-invasive means to monitor absence of recurrence following treatment.

source_records.abstract: eLife AssessmentThis is a valuable study that suggests that HPV-human DNA junctions can be identified from cfDNA in women with cervical cancer and that detection of these junctions is indicative of recurrence.The evidence supporting the conclusions is incomplete, in part because the numbers of reads identifying breakpoints in tumor samples or in circulating cell-free serum samples are not provided.More quantitative analysis will be required to confirm that the breakpoints represented in cell-free DNA can be used as a surrogate to monitor the recurrence of cervical cancer cells, and additional patient studies would also be needed to strengthen the study.This work will be of interest to those who study and treat cervical cancer as well as other HPV-related malignancies.

papers.abstract_zh: 几乎所有 宫颈癌 都是由 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 引起的。在大多数情况下,HPV DNA 会整合到人类 基因组 中。我们发现,在初始 治疗 治疗时和/或 治疗 治疗后 6 个月时,部分 宫颈癌 患者的血清游离 DNA 中可检测到肿瘤特异性 HPV-人 DNA 连接。回顾性分析显示,在癌症后来复发的女性中,这些连接更容易被检测到。我们还发现,在我们的研究和癌症 基因组 Atlas 宫颈癌 数据库中,由系统发育分支 α9 之外的 HPV 类型引起的 宫颈癌 的复发频率高于由 α9 类型引起的复发频率,尽管 宫颈癌 中 α9 类型(包括 HPV16)的 患病率 较高。因此,血清游离DNA中的HPV-人类DNA连接检测和肿瘤组织中的HPV类型测定可能有助于预测复发风险。筛查血清游离 DNA 的连接也可能提供一种明确的非侵入性方法来监测 治疗 后是否有复发。

papers.title: Predictors of anal and cervical cancer screening uptake among adults with and without HIV: survey of a community-based health clinic network.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: People with HIV (PWH) in the United States (U.S.) are disproportionately impacted by human papillomavirus-related cancers. We aimed to identify sociodemographic, health, and social predictors of anal and cervical cancer screening uptake among adults with and without HIV. METHODS: We implemented a cross-sectional survey between April and June 2024 among adult patients receiving care at a community-based clinic network (predominantly based in Florida, U.S.) that delivers HIV prevention and treatment services. Outcomes included any receipt of anal cancer screening and guideline-adherent receipt of cervical cancer screening among eligible participants. We computed adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) to identify multilevel predictors associated with screening uptake. RESULTS: Among the survey respondents, 412 (42%) were eligible for anal cancer screening and 294 (30%) for cervical cancer screening. Participants eligible for anal cancer screening included 88.8% living with HIV and 82.3% men. Men with HIV were more likely to receive anal cancer screening compared to men without HIV (aPR 1.57, 95% CI 1.08, 2.27). Among men with HIV, anal cancer screening uptake was associated with any precancer diagnosis and having three or more comorbidities. Women eligible for cervical cancer screening included 43.5% living with HIV. Women with HIV were less likely to receive guideline-adherent cervical cancer screening compared to women without HIV (aPR 0.60, 95% CI 0.47, 0.77). HIV-related disclosure concerns were associated with lower guideline-adherent cervical screening uptake among women with HIV (aPR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60, 0.94). CONCLUSION: Screening-eligible participants with HIV were more likely to receive anal cancer screening and less likely to receive cervical cancer screening. Anal and cervical cancer screening uptake differed among subpopulations of people with HIV, including by race/ethnicity, household size, any precancer, comorbidities, and HIV-related stigma. Efforts to improve anal and cervical cancer screening uptake among high-risk and screening-eligible populations are needed.

papers.title: Randomised phase III trials of cancer prevention drugs: a systematic review and prediction of trial success.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pharmacological cancer risk reduction has received far less investment than therapeutic oncology and only a few agents have entered routine practice. Understanding the predictors of positive outcomes of previous trials and issues faced is critical to future developments. METHODS: This systematic review (PROSPERO CRD420250650276) included all phase III randomised controlled trials enrolling cancer-free adults over the past 45 years, evaluating pharmacological agents and whose primary or major secondary endpoint was directly related to cancer risk reduction. To predict trials' 'success', defined here as meeting the prespecified cancer risk reduction-related endpoint within the planned timeline, we used the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator followed by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Ninety-two trials comprising 659 904 participants were included, of which 46 (50.0%) met their primary endpoint. Success rates varied by therapeutic class: vitamins (9 of 38, 23.7%), endocrine therapies (15 of 20, 75.0%), nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (8 of 13, 61.5%), human papillomavirus vaccines (8 of 9, 88.9%) and anti-infective agents (5 of 8, 62.5%). papers.title: Integrating Cervical Cancer Prevention into HIV Services in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Narrative Review Addressing the Dual Burden Among Women.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Women with HIV face a higher risk of cervical cancer. This review synthesizes evidence on precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), regional differences, risk factors, and approaches to integrating cervical cancer prevention into HIV services. METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science databases through December 2025 and identified studies evaluating the prevalence of precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in SSA. It highlights prevalence, ongoing global efforts, and integration strategies specific to SSA. RESULTS: The prevalence of precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in SSA is higher in Tanzania (71.8%), and Kenya (42%), eastern countries than from western (Nigeria, 26.6%) or southern countries (South Africa, 23.2%), influenced by the distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes, including higher-risk HPV (HR-HPV) such as HPV 35, which is not targeted by the HPV vaccine. CONCLUSIONS: Given the increased risk among women with HIV and the substantial burden in SSA, evidence suggests that integrating HPV-based cervical cancer screening and vaccination into HIV care platforms could help close the prevention gap and reduce the dual burden among women with HIV in SSA.

papers.title_zh: 将 宫颈癌 预防纳入撒哈拉以南非洲的艾滋病毒服务:解决妇女双重负担的叙述性审查。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Women with HIV face a higher risk of cervical cancer. This review synthesizes evidence on precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), regional differences, risk factors, and approaches to integrating cervical cancer prevention into HIV services. METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science databases through December 2025 and identified studies evaluating the prevalence of precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in SSA. It highlights prevalence, ongoing global efforts, and integration strategies specific to SSA. RESULTS: The prevalence of precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in SSA is higher in Tanzania (71.8%), and Kenya (42%), eastern countries than from western (Nigeria, 26.6%) or southern countries (South Africa, 23.2%), influenced by the distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes, including higher-risk HPV (HR-HPV) such as HPV 35, which is not targeted by the HPV vaccine. CONCLUSIONS: Given the increased risk among women with HIV and the substantial burden in SSA, evidence suggests that integrating HPV-based cervical cancer screening and vaccination into HIV care platforms could help close the prevention gap and reduce the dual burden among women with HIV in SSA.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:感染 HIV 的女性面临更高的 宫颈癌 风险。本综述综合了撒哈拉以南非洲 (SSA) 感染艾滋病毒的妇女中宫颈癌前病变的证据、区域差异、危险因素以及将 宫颈癌 预防纳入艾滋病毒服务的方法。方法:我们对截至 2025 年 12 月的 PubMed、Embase、Scopus 和 Web of Science 数据库进行了全面的文献检索,并确定了评估 SSA 感染 HIV 女性宫颈癌前病变 患病率 的研究。它重点介绍了 患病率、持续的全球努力以及针对 SSA 的集成策略。结果:SSA 感染 HIV 的女性中,坦桑尼亚 (71.8%) 和肯尼亚 (42%) 等东部国家的宫颈癌前病变 患病率 高于西方国家 (尼日利亚,26.6%) 或南部国家 (南非,23.2%),这受到 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 基因型分布的影响,包括高危 HPV (HR-HPV),例如 HPV 35,不是 HPV 疫苗 的目标。结论:鉴于感染艾滋病毒的女性风险增加以及 SSA 的沉重负担,有证据表明,将基于 HPV 的 宫颈癌 筛查和 疫苗接种 纳入艾滋病毒护理平台可以帮助缩小预防差距,并减轻 SSA 感染艾滋病毒的女性的双重负担。

papers.title: Protect her future: Lessons learned from a school and community engagement initiative for HPV vaccine awareness in Lilongwe, Malawi.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective strategy for preventing cervical cancer, yet vaccine uptake in Malawi remains low because of misinformation, limited awareness, and parental hesitancy. This study describes the implementation of a youth-led school and community engagement initiative to promote HPV vaccine awareness in Lilongwe, Malawi, and highlights lessons for future immunization programs. We conducted a descriptive implementation case study of a two-day youth-led engagement initiative coordinated by fellows of the 2025–2026 Global Health Corps Malawi Leadership Accelerator in collaboration with the Lilongwe District Health Office, Kawale Primary School, and partner organizations. Activities included stakeholder meetings, school health education, myth-busting sessions, learner-centered activities, community dialogs, distribution of educational materials, and on-site HPV vaccination services. Girls aged 9–14y were the primary vaccination beneficiaries, while parents, caregivers, teachers, religious leaders, and community stakeholders were engaged to strengthen vaccine acceptance. Implementation data were collected through attendance records, field notes, dialogue summaries, and reflections. Descriptive statistics and qualitative content analysis were used. The initiative reached over 500 adolescent girls through school awareness activities and engaged 45 community stakeholders across six sites. Two community dialogue sessions were conducted, 1,000 educational materials distributed, and 100 eligible girls received HPV vaccination. Community discussions identified concerns about fertility, vaccine safety, and gender targeting, while trust in health workers, school involvement, participatory dialogue, and community leader support facilitated engagement. Youth-led, community-centered engagement highlighted lessons for improving HPV vaccination through addressing misinformation, building trust, and strengthening health system readiness.

papers.title_zh: 保护她的未来:从马拉维利隆圭学校和社区参与 HPV 疫苗 意识活动中汲取的经验教训。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective strategy for preventing cervical cancer, yet vaccine uptake in Malawi remains low because of misinformation, limited awareness, and parental hesitancy. This study describes the implementation of a youth-led school and community engagement initiative to promote HPV vaccine awareness in Lilongwe, Malawi, and highlights lessons for future immunization programs. We conducted a descriptive implementation case study of a two-day youth-led engagement initiative coordinated by fellows of the 2025–2026 Global Health Corps Malawi Leadership Accelerator in collaboration with the Lilongwe District Health Office, Kawale Primary School, and partner organizations. Activities included stakeholder meetings, school health education, myth-busting sessions, learner-centered activities, community dialogs, distribution of educational materials, and on-site HPV vaccination services. Girls aged 9–14y were the primary vaccination beneficiaries, while parents, caregivers, teachers, religious leaders, and community stakeholders were engaged to strengthen vaccine acceptance. Implementation data were collected through attendance records, field notes, dialogue summaries, and reflections. Descriptive statistics and qualitative content analysis were used. The initiative reached over 500 adolescent girls through school awareness activities and engaged 45 community stakeholders across six sites. Two community dialogue sessions were conducted, 1,000 educational materials distributed, and 100 eligible girls received HPV vaccination. Community discussions identified concerns about fertility, vaccine safety, and gender targeting, while trust in health workers, school involvement, participatory dialogue, and community leader support facilitated engagement. Youth-led, community-centered engagement highlighted lessons for improving HPV vaccination through addressing misinformation, building trust, and strengthening health system readiness.

papers.title: Societal and fiscal gains from HPV vaccination in Poland - return on investment from extending access to HPV vaccination.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the societal and fiscal impact of extending the current human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination program in Poland (boys and girls aged 9-14 with average 20% vaccine coverage) by expanding age eligibility (9-17 years) and increasing vaccination coverage. METHODS: A cost-benefit analysis was conducted from both a macroeconomic (societal) and public economic (fiscal) perspective. A dynamic transmission model (DTM) was used to project the incidence and mortality of HPV-related diseases over a 100-year time horizon. Epidemiological outcomes were translated into economic outcomes using societal and fiscal frameworks incorporating productivity losses, tax revenues, and healthcare costs, and were compared with incremental vaccination costs. All costs and benefits were discounted at an annual rate of 3%. RESULTS: Compared with the current national immunization program, extending vaccination to boys and girls aged 9-17 and increasing coverage to 60% is projected to result in incremental reductions of 16% in HPV-related diseases and 13% in deaths. Achieving 90% coverage was associated with reductions of 33% in HPV-related diseases and 27% in deaths. These health gains are estimated to translate into societal benefits of EUR 4.5 billion and EUR 9.8 billion, and fiscal benefits of EUR 2.4 billion and EUR 5.1 billion, under the 60% and 90% coverage scenarios, respectively. Incremental vaccination costs are estimated at EUR 1.1 billion and EUR 2.1 billion for respective coverage scenarios. The benefit-cost analysis indicates that every EUR 1 invested yields returns of EUR 4.2 (societal) and EUR 2.2 (fiscal) at 60% coverage, and EUR 4.6 (societal) and EUR 2.4 (fiscal) at 90% coverage. All results represent incremental gains relative to the existing program. CONCLUSION: Expanding HPV vaccination eligibility and coverage in Poland is expected to generate substantial societal and fiscal returns. Higher vaccination coverage not only reduces the burden of HPV-related diseases and associated mortality but also delivers a strong and sustainable return on investment.

papers.title_zh: 波兰 HPV 疫苗接种 带来的社会和财政收益 - 扩大 HPV 疫苗接种 的使用范围带来的投资回报。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the societal and fiscal impact of extending the current human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination program in Poland (boys and girls aged 9-14 with average 20% vaccine coverage) by expanding age eligibility (9-17 years) and increasing vaccination coverage. METHODS: A cost-benefit analysis was conducted from both a macroeconomic (societal) and public economic (fiscal) perspective. A dynamic transmission model (DTM) was used to project the incidence and mortality of HPV-related diseases over a 100-year time horizon. Epidemiological outcomes were translated into economic outcomes using societal and fiscal frameworks incorporating productivity losses, tax revenues, and healthcare costs, and were compared with incremental vaccination costs. All costs and benefits were discounted at an annual rate of 3%. RESULTS: Compared with the current national immunization program, extending vaccination to boys and girls aged 9-17 and increasing coverage to 60% is projected to result in incremental reductions of 16% in HPV-related diseases and 13% in deaths. Achieving 90% coverage was associated with reductions of 33% in HPV-related diseases and 27% in deaths. These health gains are estimated to translate into societal benefits of EUR 4.5 billion and EUR 9.8 billion, and fiscal benefits of EUR 2.4 billion and EUR 5.1 billion, under the 60% and 90% coverage scenarios, respectively. Incremental vaccination costs are estimated at EUR 1.1 billion and EUR 2.1 billion for respective coverage scenarios. The benefit-cost analysis indicates that every EUR 1 invested yields returns of EUR 4.2 (societal) and EUR 2.2 (fiscal) at 60% coverage, and EUR 4.6 (societal) and EUR 2.4 (fiscal) at 90% coverage. All results represent incremental gains relative to the existing program. CONCLUSION: Expanding HPV vaccination eligibility and coverage in Poland is expected to generate substantial societal and fiscal returns. Higher vaccination coverage not only reduces the burden of HPV-related diseases and associated mortality but also delivers a strong and sustainable return on investment.

papers.title: Systemic inflammatory indices primarily reflect tumor burden rather than independently predict prognosis in HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Approximately 30% of patients with human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) have poor outcomes despite standardized treatment. Reliable biomarkers for identifying high-risk patients remain insufficiently established. UNLABELLED: To investigate the clinical significance of systemic inflammatory indices for identifying high-risk patients and to explore their associations with clinicopathological characteristics. METHODS: A total of 99 patients with HPV-associated (p16-positive) OPSCC were included. Systemic inflammatory indices, including neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), were evaluated for their associations with clinical outcomes and clinicopathological characteristics. Their prognostic significance was assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses. RESULTS: Most systemic inflammatory indices were associated with overall survival (OS) in univariate analysis, whereas only NLR was associated with progression-free survival (PFS); furthermore, none remained independently significant in multivariate analyses. Notably, all indices were significantly associated with T classification, whereas associations with N and M classifications were limited. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic inflammatory indices primarily reflected tumor burden rather than serving as independent prognostic determinants in HPV-associated OPSCC. Biomarkers derived from the local tumor immune microenvironment may provide more informative tools for risk stratification and treatment optimization.

papers.title: Developing neoantigen cancer vaccines: where are we now?
papers.abstract: The success of immunotherapies such as immune checkpoint blockade and engineered T-cells has demonstrated the immune system's anticancer potential. Although prophylactic vaccines against oncogenic viruses such as human papillomavirus prevent cancer by blocking infection, therapeutic vaccines targeting tumour-associated or tumour-specific antigens (TAAs/TSAs) have not reliably produced meaningful tumour regressions. Advances in DNA sequencing and computational pipelines for predicting individual, MHC-restricted neoantigens now enable personalized cancer vaccines (PCVs). By targeting neoantigens arising from somatic mutations, PCVs escape the central tolerance that limits anti-TAA vaccines. Multiple clinical trials have shown promise, but PCV design, delivery, and optimal disease settings require further refinement.

papers.title: Premature mortality and years of potential productive life lost due to HPV-attributable cancers in Brazil and Mexico: 2011 Versus 2023.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) remains a preventable cause of cancer mortality in Latin America. Using 2011 and 2023 mortality data from Brazil and Mexico, we estimated HPV-attributable cancer deaths, years of life lost (YLL), average YLL, and years of potential productive life lost (YPPLL) by sex, age, and cancer type, applying attributable fractions. WHO life tables were used in sensitivity analyses. HPV‐attributable deaths were higher in 2023 than in 2011, increasing from 6,515 to 9,533 in Brazil (YLL +44.6%) and from 4,303 to 4,997 in Mexico (YLL +21.4%). These absolute differences were consistent with demographic change, while age-standardized mortality rates changed more modestly. Cervical cancer dominated the burden in both countries. Among men, oropharyngeal YLL was 33.5% and 74.6% higher in Brazil and Mexico in 2023 relative to 2011; the corresponding differences for penile cancer were 54.8% and 37.7%, respectively. Anal cancer YLL showed the largest relative differences in Brazil (+159.1% in women; +203.8% in men), whereas Mexico showed a smaller difference (+32.8% in men). Although deaths were concentrated at ≥60y, substantial YLL and YPPLL occurred at younger age groups. In 2023, YPPLL totaled 97,404 y in Brazil and 51,735 y in Mexico, 43.9% and 26.7% higher than in 2011, respectively. WHO‐based sensitivity analyses yielded higher absolute YLL estimates but preserved relative patterns. These findings reveal a persistent and preventable burden of premature mortality and YPPLL from HPV‐attributable cancers in Brazil and Mexico, underscoring the need for expanded HPV vaccination, screening, timely diagnosis, and equitable treatment across affected cancer sites.

Using 2011 and 2023 mortality data from Brazil and Mexico, we estimated HPV-attributable cancer deaths, years of life lost (YLL), average YLL, and years of potential productive life lost (YPPLL) by sex, age, and cancer type, applying attributable fractions. WHO life tables were used in sensitivity analyses. HPV‐attributable deaths were higher in 2023 than in 2011, increasing from 6,515 to 9,533 in Brazil (YLL +44.6%) and from 4,303 to 4,997 in Mexico (YLL +21.4%). These absolute differences were consistent with demographic change, while age-standardized mortality rates changed more modestly. Cervical cancer dominated the burden in both countries. Among men, oropharyngeal YLL was 33.5% and 74.6% higher in Brazil and Mexico in 2023 relative to 2011; the corresponding differences for penile cancer were 54.8% and 37.7%, respectively. Anal cancer YLL showed the largest relative differences in Brazil (+159.1% in women; +203.8% in men), whereas Mexico showed a smaller difference (+32.8% in men). Although deaths were concentrated at ≥60y, substantial YLL and YPPLL occurred at younger age groups. In 2023, YPPLL totaled 97,404 y in Brazil and 51,735 y in Mexico, 43.9% and 26.7% higher than in 2011, respectively. WHO‐based sensitivity analyses yielded higher absolute YLL estimates but preserved relative patterns. These findings reveal a persistent and preventable burden of premature mortality and YPPLL from HPV‐attributable cancers in Brazil and Mexico, underscoring the need for expanded HPV vaccination, screening, timely diagnosis, and equitable treatment across affected cancer sites.

papers.abstract_zh: 在拉丁美洲,人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 仍然是可预防的癌症 死亡率。使用来自巴西和墨西哥的 2011 年和 2023 年 死亡率 数据,我们应用归因分数,按性别、年龄和癌症类型估计了 HPV 归因的癌症死亡、寿命损失年数 (YLL)、平均 YLL 和潜在生产性寿命损失年数 (YPPLL)。世界卫生组织生命表用于敏感性分析。2023 年 HPV 导致的死亡人数高于 2011 年,巴西从 6,515 人增加到 9,533 人(YLL +44.6%),墨西哥从 4,303 人增加到 4,997 人(YLL +21.4%)。这些绝对差异与人口变化一致,而年龄标准化的 死亡率 比率变化较小。宫颈癌 主导了两国的负担。在男性中,2023 年巴西和墨西哥的口咽部 YLL 较 2011 年分别高出 33.5% 和 74.6%;阴茎癌的相应差异分别为 54.8% 和 37.7%。巴西肛门癌 YLL 的相对差异最大(女性 +159.1%;男性 +203.8%),而墨西哥的差异较小(男性 +32.8%)。尽管死亡集中在≥60岁,但大量的YLL和YPPLL发生在较年轻的年龄组。2023年,巴西YPPLL总数为97,404年,墨西哥为51,735年,分别比2011年增长43.9%和26.7%。基于 WHO 的敏感性分析得出了更高的绝对 YLL 估计值,但保留了相对模式。这些发现揭示了巴西和墨西哥因 HPV 相关癌症导致的早产 死亡率 和 YPPLL 的负担持续且可预防,这强调了在受影响的癌症部位扩大 HPV 疫苗接种、筛查、及时 诊断 和公平 治疗 的必要性。

papers.title: HPV e o colo do útero: uma revisão sistemática sobre epidemiologia e impacto clínico de pesquisadores envolvidos.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most prevalent sexually transmitted infections worldwide and plays a central role in the etiology of cervical cancer. Although most HPV infections are transient and spontaneously cleared by the immune system, persistent infection with oncogenic HPV types, particularly genotypes 16 and 18, may lead to progressive intraepithelial lesions that can evolve into invasive carcinoma in the absence of timely diagnosis and treatment. Cervical cancer remains an important public health problem, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where inequalities in access to vaccination, screening, and treatment contribute to persistent high incidence and mortality rates. This study aimed to analyze, through a systematic review of the literature, the epidemiology of HPV infection, its relationship with the development of cervical precursor lesions and cancer, and its main clinical and public health impacts. The review was structured according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) recommendations, including epidemiological studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, and technical-scientific documents related to HPV infection, cervical cancer, vaccination, and screening strategies. Epidemiological evidence demonstrates a wide global distribution of HPV infection, with variations according to age, geographic region, and population characteristics. Persistent infection with high-risk HPV constitutes a necessary condition for the development of most cervical cancers, although carcinogenesis also depends on host-related, behavioral, immunological, and socioeconomic cofactors. HPV vaccination and screening for precursor lesions are the main prevention strategies. In Brazil, the progressive implementation of molecular testing for oncogenic HPV DNA represents an important change in the national cervical cancer screening strategy. It is concluded that cervical cancer control requires integration of vaccination, screening, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up, together with efforts to reduce inequalities in access to healthcare services.

papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 是全球最流行的性传播感染之一,在 宫颈癌 的病因学中发挥着核心作用。虽然大多数 HPV 感染是暂时性的,并会被免疫系统自发清除,但致癌 HPV 类型(尤其是基因型 16 和 18)的持续感染可能会导致进行性上皮内病变,如果没有及时 诊断 和 治疗,可能会演变成浸润性癌。宫颈癌 仍然是一个重要的公共卫生问题,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家,这些国家在获得 疫苗接种、筛查和 治疗 方面的不平等导致 发病率 和 死亡率 比率持续居高不下。本研究旨在通过系统回顾文献,分析HPV感染的流行病学、其与宫颈前驱病变和癌症发展的关系,以及其主要的临床和公共卫生影响。该综述是根据系统评价和荟萃分析的首选报告项目(PRISMA 2020)建议构建的,包括流行病学研究、系统评价、荟萃分析、临床试验以及与 HPV 感染、宫颈癌、疫苗接种 和筛查策略相关的技术科学文件。流行病学证据表明,HPV 感染在全球范围内广泛分布,并根据年龄、地理区域和人口特征而存在差异。高危型HPV 的持续感染构成了大多数 宫颈癌 发展的必要条件,尽管致癌也取决于 宿主 相关的、行为的、免疫学的和社会经济的辅助因素。HPV 疫苗接种 和前驱病变筛查是主要的预防策略。在巴西,致癌 HPV DNA 分子检测的逐步实施代表了国家 宫颈癌 筛查策略的重要变化。结论是,宫颈癌 控制需要整合 疫苗接种、筛查、诊断、治疗 和后续行动,并努力减少获得医疗服务的不平等。

(2017), in a cross-sectional study of the NHANES 2013-2014 dataset, overall genital HPV infection prevalence among 1,868 men was observed to be 45.2%, widespread across all age groups, alongside a low HPV vaccination rate of 10.7%. • Available literature indicates that genital HPV prevalence is higher in men than in women. Request for Unlocking the Sample Page of the Human Papillomavirus Treatment Market @ https://www.delveinsight.com/sample-request/human-papillomavirus-hpv-market?utm_source=openpr&utm_medium=pressrelease&utm_campaign=akpr What is Human Papillomavirus? Human Papillomavirus is the most common DNA virus that causes infection in the epithelial cells of skin and mucosa. The moist epithelial surfaces (squamous cells) include all areas covered by skin and/or mucosa, such as the mouth interior, throat, tongue, tonsils, vagina, cervix, (the urethra opening), and anus. Contact with these areas leads to transmission of the virus, allowing it to transfer between epithelial cells. While sexual contact, both conventional and oral, is a known means of transferring HPV through direct skin-to-skin contact, other possible pathways for transfer of the virus are still poorly understood. HPV can cause cervical and other cancers, including cancer of vagina, or anus, and can also cause cancer in the back of the throat, including the base of the tongue and tonsils (oropharyngeal cancer). Cancer often takes years, even decades, to develop after a person acquires HPV. Additionally, the HPV types that cause genital warts are not the same as the types that cause cancers. This part of the report also provides the diagnosed patient pool and their trends along with assumptions undertaken, covering the United States, EU5 countries (Germany, Spain, Italy, France, and the United Kingdom), and Japan from 2020 to 2034. Download the report to understand which factors are driving Human Papillomavirus epidemiology trends @ https://www.delveinsight.com/report-store/human-papillomavirus-hpv-market?utm_source=openpr&utm_medium=pressrelease&utm_campaign=akpr Human Papillomavirus Diagnosis and Human Papillomavirus Treatment Human Papillomavirus (HPV) diagnosis involves screening and diagnostic tests to identify high-risk HPV infections and detect abnormal cervical cell changes. Common approaches include HPV DNA testing, HPV mRNA testing, and Pap tests, often used together for cervical cancer screening. Human Papillomavirus treatment depends on the condition and symptoms, as there is no specific treatment that eliminates the virus itself. Management may include monitoring, topical therapies, cryotherapy, surgical removal, or other procedures for HPV-related warts and precancerous lesions. Human Papillomavirus Emerging Drugs The Human Papillomavirus therapeutics market report provides the details of the emerging therapies under the late and mid-stage of development for Human Papillomavirus treatment. • VGX-3100: Inovio Pharmaceuticals, Inc. VGX-3100 is an investigational immunotherapy designed to treat precancers and cancers caused by Human Papillomavirus. The drug is in Phase III development for HPV-associated precancerous cervical dysplasia. It eliminated high-grade dysplasia in nearly 50% of women in a Phase IIb clinical trial, and in 80% of those whose high-grade dysplasia was eliminated, the HPV infection was also cleared by VGX-3100. High-risk HPV is responsible for 70% of cervical cancer, 91% of anal cancer, and 69% of vulvar cancer. Using ASPIRE technology, VGX-3100 includes DNA plasmids targeting the E6 and E7 proteins of HPV types 16 and 18, delivered intramuscularly using the CELLECTRA 5PSP delivery device. Inovio Pharmaceuticals is also investigating INO-3107 for treatment of recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) caused by HPV types 6 and 11 infections. • ISA101: ISA Pharmaceuticals/Regeneron Pharmaceuticals ISA101 (HPV16) consists of 12 long synthetic peptides (25-35 amino acids long) derived from the E6 and E7 oncogenic proteins of the HPV16 virus, a strain responsible for over 50% of human cervical cancers and cervical intraepithelial neoplasias, more than 85% of HPV-positive head and neck cancers, and various other HPV-related disorders. ISA101 is believed to target the gap between prophylactic vaccines and standard-of-care cancer treatments. It has completed a Phase II trial in vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia, establishing clinical proof-of-concept, and in cervical cancer has successfully completed a company-sponsored Phase I/II trial, entering further clinical development in collaboration with Regeneron. Human Papillomavirus is the most common DNA virus that causes infection in the epithelial cells of skin and mucosa. The moist epithelial surfaces (squamous cells) include all areas covered by skin and/or mucosa, such as the mouth interior, throat, tongue, tonsils, vagina, cervix, (the urethra opening), and anus. Contact with these areas leads to transmission of the virus, allowing it to transfer between epithelial cells. While sexual contact, both conventional and oral, is a known means of transferring HPV through direct skin-to-skin contact, other possible pathways for transfer of the virus are still poorly understood. HPV can cause cervical and other cancers, including cancer of vagina, or anus, and can also cause cancer in the back of the throat, including the base of the tongue and tonsils (oropharyngeal cancer). Cancer often takes years, even decades, to develop after a person acquires HPV. Additionally, the HPV types that cause genital warts are not the same as the types that cause cancers. Common approaches include HPV DNA testing, HPV mRNA testing, and Pap tests, often used together for cervical cancer screening. Human Papillomavirus treatment depends on the condition and symptoms, as there is no specific treatment that eliminates the virus itself. Management may include monitoring, topical therapies, cryotherapy, surgical removal, or other procedures for HPV-related warts and precancerous lesions. VGX-3100 is an investigational immunotherapy designed to treat precancers and cancers caused by Human Papillomavirus. The drug is in Phase III development for HPV-associated precancerous cervical dysplasia. It eliminated high-grade dysplasia in nearly 50% of women in a Phase IIb clinical trial, and in 80% of those whose high-grade dysplasia was eliminated, the HPV infection was also cleared by VGX-3100. High-risk HPV is responsible for 70% of cervical cancer, 91% of anal cancer, and 69% of vulvar cancer. Using ASPIRE technology, VGX-3100 includes DNA plasmids targeting the E6 and E7 proteins of HPV types 16 and 18, delivered intramuscularly using the CELLECTRA 5PSP delivery device. Inovio Pharmaceuticals is also investigating INO-3107 for treatment of recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) caused by HPV types 6 and 11 infections. • ISA101: ISA Pharmaceuticals/Regeneron Pharmaceuticals ISA101 (HPV16) consists of 12 long synthetic peptides (25-35 amino acids long) derived from the E6 and E7 oncogenic proteins of the HPV16 virus, a strain responsible for over 50% of human cervical cancers and cervical intraepithelial neoplasias, more than 85% of HPV-positive head and neck cancers, and various other HPV-related disorders. ISA101 is believed to target the gap between prophylactic vaccines and standard-of-care cancer treatments. It has completed a Phase II trial in vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia, establishing clinical proof-of-concept, and in cervical cancer has successfully completed a company-sponsored Phase I/II trial, entering further clinical development in collaboration with Regeneron. news.content_zh: 在认识提高、疫苗 开发进步以及针对靶向治疗的持续研究的推动下,人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 市场将出现大幅增长。2026 年 8 月,Labo'Life 公布了一项评估 2LPAPI® 在清除生殖器高危 (HR) HPV 感染方面的功效的研究结果。2026 年 7 月,Fred Hutchinson 癌症中心分享了 IMPACT HPV 研究的结果,该研究重点关注药房中的 HPV 疫苗接种 教育。该报告强调,HPV 是美国最常见的性传播感染,18-69 岁成年人中任何口腔 HPV 感染者中,患病率 占 7.3%,高危型HPV 占 4.0%。高危型HPV 与 70% 的 宫颈癌、91% 的肛门癌和 69% 的外阴癌相关。该报告还讨论了 VGX-3100 和 ISA101 等新兴疗法,这些疗法针对特定的 HPV 类型,并处于临床开发的不同阶段。这些调查结果基于市场分析和流行病学数据,并非已证实的 暴发 事件。

analysis_zh.time: 2026 年 8 月,Labo'Life 公布了一项研究结果;2026 年 7 月,弗雷德·哈钦森癌症中心公布了一项研究结果。据报道,2020 年至 2034 年市场将持续增长。
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 美国、欧盟五国(德国、西班牙、意大利、法国和英国)和日本是分析的七个主要市场(7MM)。报告还提到了美国 18-69 岁成年人的 患病率 数据以及 NHANES 2013-2014 数据集中针对男性的横断面研究。
analysis_zh.event: Labo'Life 进行了一项随机、安慰剂对照、双盲研究,以评估 2LPAPI® 清除生殖器 HR-HPV 感染的功效。Fred Hutchinson 癌症中心在药房实施了积极主动的 HPV 疫苗接种 交流和教学方法:IMPACT HPV 研究。由于认识的提高、疫苗 开发的进步以及对靶向治疗的持续研究,人乳头瘤病毒 市场正在经历大幅增长。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 由于认识的提高、疫苗 开发的进步以及对靶向治疗的持续研究,市场增长显着。高危型HPV 导致 70% 的 宫颈癌、91% 的肛门癌和 69% 的外阴癌。美国 18-69 岁成年人任何口腔 HPV 的 患病率 为 7.3%,而 高危型HPV 为 4.0%。

analysis.location_and_population: The announcement concerns Paraguay. It targets adolescent females aged 15‐18 who have not previously received HPV vaccination, and extends free vaccination to all persons under 18. Priority groups for free vaccine include HIV‐positive individuals, patients on immunosuppressive therapy, organ‐transplant recipients, survivors of sexual violence, and those diagnosed with cervical CIN2 lesions.
analysis.event: Paraguay’s health ministry launched a new HPV vaccination strategy that offers the vaccine free of charge to eligible youths under 18, especially females 15‐18 who missed earlier doses. The policy also broadens eligibility to people under 45 who are at higher risk of persistent infection or disease recurrence. The announcement is an official government statement, not a disease outbreak, and is confirmed by the ministry’s communication.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The report does not provide case or death counts. It states that the vaccine is the most effective preventive tool and is expected to markedly lower future HPV‐related tumor risk, but no quantitative impact is given.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Free vaccines are now available through authorized medical facilities nationwide. Health workers will verify eligibility using an electronic vaccination registry or physical cards. The ministry emphasizes ongoing implementation and monitoring, with no unresolved questions reported in the article.

analysis.brief_en: Paraguay’s health ministry announced on September 6, 2026 a new HPV vaccination program that makes the vaccine free for adolescents under 18, focusing on girls aged 15‐18 who missed earlier doses. The initiative also expands eligibility to high‐risk groups under 45, such as HIV‐positive patients, organ‐transplant recipients, and those with cervical precancerous lesions. Authorized clinics across the country will dispense the vaccine, confirming eligibility via an electronic registry or paper cards. Officials stress that the vaccine remains the most effective tool to prevent future HPV‐related cancers, though the announcement provides no specific case numbers or impact metrics. The policy is a confirmed government measure aimed at reducing cervical cancer burden in Paraguay.

Show results from: Clear search input Search for result Max Clear search input Search for result Press release Papua New Guinea launches HPV vaccination to protect girls from cervical cancer Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths for women in Papua New Guinea, with over 1,000 women diagnosed and ~650 deaths annually. 07 September 2026 UNICEF PNG PORT MORESBY, 8 September 2026 – The Government of Papua New Guinea today introduced human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination into its national immunization programme, taking a major step towards protecting future generations of girls and women from cervical cancer, currently the leading cause of cancer deaths among women in the country. At a national launch at New Erima Primary School in Port Moresby, trained health workers vaccinated eligible girls aged 9-14 with the first doses. Following the launch, Phase 1 of the programme will begin free of charge across the National Capital District (NCD) and Central Province in November 2026, before gradually expanding to other provinces. Cervical cancer is the leading cause of cancer deaths among women in Papua New Guinea. Over 1,000 women are diagnosed with the disease and approximately 650 die of it each year. Yet cervical cancer is largely preventable. More than 95 per cent of cervical cancer is caused by HPV. Vaccinating girls before exposure to the virus can protect them against HPV strains responsible for up to 90 per cent of cervical cancer cases. The programme expects to reach about 60,000 eligible girls in the first phase of the campaign. The vaccination campaign will be implemented through school-based vaccination as well as health facilities and community outreach to ensure broader and equitable access, so that girls who are out of school or live far from services are not left behind. Since schools are the main delivery channel, Government-led preparedness and response will be essential to keep them open. El Niño is projected to place further pressure on water supplies across Papua New Guinea. Severe shortages could disrupt learning and force schools to close. Safe water provides a healthy learning environment and reduces the spread of disease. This factor is especially important for girls, enabling them to manage menstruation with dignity, attend school and access vaccination. The HPV vaccine is safe, effective and recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO). Beginning in 2006, more than 162 countries worldwide have introduced national HPV vaccination programmes, helping to protect millions of lives. With Gavi support, 95 million girls have been protected in lower-and middle-income countries alone, helping to avert an estimated 1.9 million future deaths from cervical cancer. In Papua New Guinea, girls aged 9-14 years will receive a single dose of the HPV vaccine, providing protection before potential exposure to the virus. The National Department of Health is leading the vaccination programme in collaboration with the National Department of Education and Provincial Health Authorities. The introduction of the HPV vaccine is supported by the Australian Government; Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance (Gavi); WHO; and UNICEF. Schools, churches, health workers, community leaders and families will help the programme reach girls across the targeted provinces. As the programme expands, sustained national leadership, partnership and investment will be essential. This includes reliable vaccine supplies and cold-chain systems, trained health workers, effective delivery through schools and communities, trusted information, and robust data to identify girls who might otherwise be missed. HPV vaccination remains the most effective way to prevent HPV infection, while cervical cancer screening and treatment remain essential for women across the life-cycle. Together, vaccination, screening and treatment have significantly reduced cervical cancer deaths globally. Parents and caregivers are encouraged to follow information from schools, health facilities and outreach teams, ask trained health workers if they have questions and concerns, and make sure eligible girls are vaccinated when services reach their communities. Notes For editors: The Papua New Guinea HPV vaccine launch on September 8, 2026, brought together Secretary for Health Mr Pascoe Kase, Deputy Secretary for Education Ms Sabati Mero, National Capital District Governor Hon. Powes Parkop, the Australian Government’s Minister-Counsellor Ms Madeleine Moss, Gavi Chief Executive Officer Dr Sania Nishtar, WHO Representative Dr Rajendra-Prasad Yadav and UNICEF Representative Dr Veera Mendonca. Students, teachers, health workers, faith and community leaders, partners and members of the media also attended. Quotations from key leaders and partners Hon. Dr Billy Joseph, Minister for Health, Government of Papua New Guinea “Cervical cancer is taking too many women from their families and communities. Today’s launch begins the work of making this protection available to girls across Papua New Guinea. We will start in the National Capital District and Central Province, review the data and service quality, learn from delivery and strengthen the programme as it expands.” Mr Pascoe Kase, Secretary for Health, National Department of Health “For the first time, girls in Papua New Guinea will have access to a vaccine that can protect them from cervical cancer later in life. Our job now is to make sure that protection reaches every eligible girl, including those who are not in school or live far from health services. This is an investment in the health of the next generation of PNG women.” Dr Uke Kombra, Secretary, National Department of Education, Government of Papua New Guinea “Schools can bring this protection close to most eligible girls. Teachers and school leaders will help families understand when and where vaccination is available, support safe school vaccination sessions and follow up with girls who miss the first opportunity. Our partnership with health services is essential to reaching girls in every school community.” Hon. Powes Pakop, Governor, National Capital District “Young people are at the heart of NCD’s future. The NCD Government has a responsibility to make sure every girl can access services that protect her health and support her future. Launching HPV vaccination here in Port Moresby puts that responsibility into action. We will work through our schools, health services and communities to build confidence and reach every eligible girl across the city, especially those who might otherwise be missed.” H.E. Ewen McDonald AM, Australian High Commissioner to Papua New Guinea and Special Envoy for the Pacific and Regional Affairs “Australia and Papua New Guinea are close neighbours and enduring partners. We stand together in building stronger health systems and a healthier future for the people of Papua New Guinea. The introduction of HPV vaccination reflects what this partnership can achieve. Australia remains committed to working alongside the Government and its partners over the long term to protect women and girls and strengthen the services that communities depend upon.” Dr Sania Nishtar, Chief Executive Officer, Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance "With just one dose of the HPV vaccine, we can give a girl lasting protection against cervical cancer and the chance of a healthier future. Today's introduction of the HPV vaccine marks an important moment of progress and, with Gavi’s support, Papua New Guinea joins a growing global effort to protect more girls and save lives.” Dr Rajendra-Prasad Yadav, WHO Representative to Papua New Guinea “Cervical cancer is one of the few cancers we have the tools to prevent. HPV vaccination, a proven success globally, gives Papua New Guinea an opportunity to protect its girls against cervical cancer later in life. Combined with screening and treatment for women, high vaccination coverage can put the country on the path towards eventually eliminating cervical cancer as a public health problem. WHO commends the Government of Papua New Guinea on this milestone, demonstrating foresight and commitment to strengthening health for all.” Dr Veera Mendonca, UNICEF Representative to Papua New Guinea “Today’s launch is only the beginning. Success will be measured by whether every eligible girl receives the vaccine safely and on time, and whether families can access accurate information. Schools are central to delivery, so Government-led preparedness and response will be essential to keep them open as El Niño places greater pressure on water supplies. Safe water and sanitation are especially important for girls’ health, dignity and attendance. UNICEF has supported the quality-assured procurement and delivery of HPV vaccines and will continue working with the Government and partners to reach girls who may be missed and sustain vaccination through routine immunisation,” said Dr Veera Mendonca, UNICEF Representative to Papua New Guinea. Media contacts Pravaran Mahat Chief, Advocacy and Communications UNICEF Papua New Guinea Tel: +675 7979 9364 Email: pmahat@unicef.org About UNICEF UNICEF promotes the rights and wellbeing of every child, in everything we do. Together with our partners, we work across Papua New Guinea to translate that commitment into practical action, focusing special effort on reaching the most vulnerable and excluded children, to the benefit of all children, everywhere. analysis.time: The Government of Papua New Guinea introduced the HPV vaccination programme on 8 September 2026, with Phase 1 beginning in November 2026 across the National Capital District (NCD) and Central Province.
analysis.location_and_population: The programme is being implemented in Papua New Guinea, specifically targeting girls aged 9-14 years in the National Capital District (NCD) and Central Province, with plans to expand to other provinces.
analysis.event: Papua New Guinea launched an HPV vaccination programme to protect girls from cervical cancer, as reported by the Government of Papua New Guinea and UNICEF. This is a confirmed event based on the official press release.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The programme aims to reach about 60,000 eligible girls in the first phase. Cervical cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women in Papua New Guinea, with over 1,000 women diagnosed and approximately 650 deaths annually. Over 95% of cervical cancer cases are caused by HPV, and the vaccine is expected to protect against strains responsible for up to 90% of cases.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The vaccination campaign is being implemented through school-based delivery, health facilities, and community outreach. The National Department of Health is leading the programme in collaboration with the National Department of Education and Provincial Health Authorities. The programme is under review and will expand gradually, with ongoing efforts to ensure reliable vaccine supplies, trained health workers, and effective delivery.

analysis.brief_en: Papua New Guinea launched an HPV vaccination programme on 8 September 2026, aiming to protect girls from cervical cancer, which is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women in the country. Over 1,000 women are diagnosed with cervical cancer annually, with approximately 650 deaths. The programme, introduced by the Government of Papua New Guinea and supported by UNICEF, will initially target girls aged 9-14 in the National Capital District (NCD) and Central Province, with plans to expand to other provinces. The first phase, starting in November 2026, will provide free vaccinations, with efforts to ensure equitable access through schools, health facilities, and community outreach. The National Department of Health is leading the initiative in collaboration with the National Department of Education and Provincial Health Authorities. The HPV vaccine is safe and effective, and its introduction is expected to significantly reduce cervical cancer cases and deaths. The programme emphasizes the importance of sustained national leadership, reliable vaccine supplies, and trained health workers to ensure success.

news.source_body_en: Papua New Guinea launched an HPV vaccination programme on 8 September 2026, aiming to protect girls from cervical cancer, which is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women in the country. Over 1,000 women are diagnosed with cervical cancer annually, with approximately 650 deaths. The programme, introduced by the Government of Papua New Guinea and supported by UNICEF, will initially target girls aged 9-14 in the National Capital District (NCD) and Central Province, with plans to expand to other provinces. The first phase, starting in November 2026, will provide free vaccinations, with efforts to ensure equitable access through schools, health facilities, and community outreach. The National Department of Health is leading the initiative in collaboration with the National Department of Education and Provincial Health Authorities. The HPV vaccine is safe and effective, and its introduction is expected to significantly reduce cervical cancer cases and deaths. The programme emphasizes the importance of sustained national leadership, reliable vaccine supplies, and trained health workers to ensure success.

news.content: Dinamani Kannada Prabha Samakalika Malayalam Cinema Express Indulgexpress Edexlive Sep 11, 2026 9:53 PM Subscribe E-PAPER INDIA WORLD STATES CITIES OPINION EXPLAINER BUSINESS SPORTS GOOD NEWS ENTERTAINMENT VIDEOS LIVE BLOG INDIA WORLD STATES CITIES OPINION EXPLAINER BUSINESS SPORTS GOOD NEWS ENTERTAINMENT VIDEOS LIVE BLOG Trending Links Speaker J C D Prabhakar TVK Government Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Sanjay Jha Vinesh Phogat Advertisement India India crosses over 80 lakh HPV vaccinations in its fight against cervical cancer Under the campaign, 14-year-old girls are provided voluntary and free-of-cost single-dose vaccination against human papillomavirus (HPV), an infection that causes cervical cancer, which is the second most common cancer among women in the country. Among states, Uttar Pradesh has recorded the highest number of vaccinations, with more than 22 lakh adolescent girls vaccinated under the campaign.(Photo | ANI) Kavita Bajeli-Datt Updated on: 11 Sep 2026, 1:11 pm 3 min read Copied NEW DELHI: In its efforts to prevent cervical cancer, India has administered over 80 lakh doses of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine under the National HPV Vaccination Campaign over the past six months, officials said Friday. Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram have achieved 100 per cent coverage of their respective identified target populations, while Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Assam have crossed 90 per cent coverage, officials added. While Karnataka has achieved more than 85 per cent coverage, Chhattisgarh, Sikkim, Kerala, Telangana and Odisha have crossed 60 per cent coverage, they added. Among states, Uttar Pradesh has recorded the highest number of vaccinations, with more than 22 lakh adolescent girls vaccinated under the campaign. “The milestone marks the expanding reach of HPV vaccination through the public health system and reinforces India’s commitment to strengthening preventive healthcare for adolescent girls,” the officials added. The National HPV Vaccination Campaign was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on February 28. Under the campaign, 14-year-old girls are provided voluntary and free-of-cost single-dose vaccination against human papillomavirus (HPV), an infection that causes cervical cancer, which is the second most common cancer among women in the country. The vaccination is given with parental consent at government health facilities. All vaccination sessions under the campaign are conducted under the supervision of trained medical officers. “Government health facilities are also linked with 24×7 healthcare facilities...following Immunization (AEFI). This mechanism ensures timely assessment, monitoring and management of any vaccination-related adverse event,” mentioned a statement from the Union Health Ministry. As per Registrar General of India (RGI) 2021 estimates, approximately 1.2 crore girls constitute the annual cohort of 14-year-olds who are expected to benefit from the initiative each year. Andhra Pradesh records 98.47 per cent HPV coverage As many states have made significant progress in expanding HPV vaccination coverage, the officials said this “progress reflects coordinated implementation by states and union territories, sustained community mobilisation and active engagement of district-level health teams.” States have adopted context-specific approaches to reach eligible adolescent girls through the public health delivery network, including in rural, urban, remote and geographically challenging areas, they said. Officials pointed out that MP and Gujarat have achieved 100 per cent coverage of their identified target cohorts, supported by sustained community mobilisation, coordinated implementation and focused field-level efforts. The progress in Assam and other northeastern states also demonstrates the role of integrated community health networks and coordinated field-level action in expanding access across geographically diverse areas. The campaign has placed strong emphasis on community engagement and credible information, with parents, healthcare providers, teachers and frontline health workers being actively engaged to address concerns and counter misinformation relating to HPV vaccination. Healthcare providers, including paediatricians, gynaecologists and experts from institutions such as AIIMS, along with teachers and frontline health workers including ASHAs and ANMs, have supported awareness and mobilisation efforts across states and districts. “The campaign has also leveraged India’s digital health infrastructure through the U-WIN platform, enabling programme managers to monitor vaccination coverage at the district level, identify coverage gaps and missed beneficiaries, and support more effective programme planning and resource allocation,” the statement said. “The national campaign builds on extensive global experience with HPV vaccination,” it added. More than 800 million doses of HPV vaccines have been distributed globally, providing substantial real-world experience on their use and safety. HPV vaccination, initially adopted predominantly by high-income countries, has progressively expanded into national immunisation programmes across countries at different income levels. At present, 87 per cent of upper-middle-income countries, 78 per cent of lower-middle-income countries and 54 per cent of low-income countries have adopted HPV vaccines in their National Immunization Programmes. The growing adoption of HPV vaccination across diverse income settings reflects its increasing role as an important component of national strategies for cervical cancer prevention, the statement said. With the campaign progressing towards its final phase, the focus remains on reaching the remaining eligible beneficiaries and ensuring that no eligible girl is left behind. “The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare continues to work closely with states and union territories, healthcare professionals, frontline health workers and communities to strengthen awareness, facilitate access and support effective implementation of the HPV Vaccination Campaign,” the statement said. The statement added that achievement of 80 lakh HPV vaccine doses marks an important step in India’s efforts to strengthen preventive healthcare and advance long-term protection against cervical cancer among future generations. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), cervical cancer is the fifth most commonly diagnosed cancer in women globally with around 6,04,000 new cases and around 2,80,000 deaths in 2024. It is largely preventable through HPV vaccination and regular screening and it can be cured if detected early and treated promptly. India reports over 1,20,000 new cases and nearly 80,000 fatalities from cervical cancer each year, according to the 2022 WHO GLOBOCAN report.
